prompt: Kofi does practice questions every evening, but after about five seconds on each one he flips to the answer, nods, and moves on. A week later he can recognise the answers but cannot produce them in a test. Why is his 'testing' practice failing?

options.text: Practice questions only work if they are done in the morning, when memory is freshest
He never makes a genuine retrieval attempt before seeing the answer, so he practises recognising answers rather than recalling them
The questions are too easy, because he eventually understands every answer he reads
Testing only works for factual subjects, not for the kind of material he is studying

explanation: The testing effect depends on trying to retrieve the answer from memory before feedback. Closing the book, writing an answer, and only then checking turns each question into real retrieval practice.
